Question 2: Do students who ranked themselves as more comfortable with programming, more likely to prefer R or Python?    
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
interest_data <- read.csv("/Users/ryanchang377/pstat197a/module0-class-survey-team3/data/interest-clean.csv")

background_data <- read.csv("/Users/ryanchang377/pstat197a/module0-class-survey-team3/data/background-clean.csv")

data <- inner_join(interest_data, background_data, by ="response_id")
data

data %>%
  group_by(language) %>%
  summarize(count = n(), mean_comfortability = mean(prog.comf, na.rm = TRUE), 
            median_comfortability = median(prog.comf, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_comfortability = sd(prog.comf, na.rm = TRUE))

```
```{r}
language_data <- data %>%
  filter(language %in% c("Python", "R")) %>%
  mutate(preferR = ifelse(language == "R", 1,0))

logistic_model <- glm(preferR ~ prog.comf, data = language_data, family = binomial)
summary(logistic_model)
```
According to the logistic regression model, prog.comf has a -0.4939 coefficient, meaning for every level increase of comfortability in programming, the log odds for preferring R over python shrinks by that much. While this would support the claim that students who are more comfortable programming prefer python over R, the p value (0.299) is much higher than 0.05, which means that this relationship is not statstically significant.


```{r}


ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(prog.comf), fill = language)) + geom_bar(position = "fill", width = 0.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) + scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Python" = "blue", "R" = "red", "No preference" = "grey"),
    name = "Language Preference") +
  labs(title = "Proportion of Language Preference by Programming Comfort",
    x = "Programming Comfort Level",
    y = "Percentage of Group") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) 
```
This bar plot visually shows that the distribution of students who prefer python are definitely left skewed, while the distribution of students who prfer R are right skewed. This could support the idea that students who are more comfortable with programming prefer python over R.
